top_evidence.text: Data extraction was independently conducted by two reviewers using a standardized form. Any discrepancies were resolved through discussion or consultation with a third reviewer. For each primary study, we collected first author, year, country, study design, sample size, number of ERCP procedures, mean or median age, ERCP indications, procedure type, follow-up duration, adverse-event definitions or reporting windows, event numerators and denominators for PEP, bleeding, perforation, cholangitis or infection, severity classification, risk factors, and management strategies. For PEP, we recorded whether the denominator represented ERCP procedures, patients, first ERCP per child, or a mixed/unclear reporting unit. We retained the denominator unit used by the source rather than converting procedure-level data to patient-level data when repeat procedures per child were not consistently reported. top_evidence.text: This systematic review included 65 sources in the qualitative synthesis, consisting primarily of contemporary pediatric ERCP primary studies and selected prior systematic reviews or meta-analyses used for contextual benchmarking[2-14, 19-71]. Prior reviews were not treated as independent primary data and their pooled estimates were not combined with overlapping primary studies. A detailed account of the literature screening and selection process, following PRISMA 2020 principles, is illustrated in Figure 1.

top_evidence.text:
Table 3. Prevention and management strategies for post-ERCP complications in children

| Complication   | Prevention                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                       | Management                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    |
|----------------|------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| PEP            | Risk stratification by age, indication, prior pancreatitis, and anticipated pancreatic manipulation; minimize pancreatic duct cannulation and contrast injection; selective prophylactic pancreatic stenting after high-risk pancreatic instrumentation with stent caliber and length matched to pancreatic duct size and child size; NSAID prophylaxis only after checking age, weight, renal function, bleeding risk, and local pediatric protocols; monitored hydration; experienced pediatric ERCP operator. | Conservative care with intravenous fluids, analgesia, antiemetics, and early enteral nutrition when feasible; intensive monitoring for systemic inflammatory response; drainage or debridement only for selected infected necrosis or persistent collections. |
| Bleeding       | Correct coagulopathy or thrombocytopenia before ERCP when possible; review antiplatelet or anticoagulant exposure; use careful sphincterotomy or papillotomy technique; consider selective prophylactic hemostasis in high-risk lesions. IN                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                      | Endoscopic injection, clipping, or thermal coagulation; transfusion when unstable; angiographic embolization or surgery for refractory cases. PRESS                                                                                                           |
| Perforation    | Meticulous cannulation, avoidance of excessive guidewire or endoscope force, recognition of altered anatomy, and early senior-operator takeover during difficult access. ARTICLE                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                 | Conservative care for selected small retroperitoneal perforations; endoscopic closure in selected cases; surgical repair for large defects, free perforation, or peritonitis.                                                                                 |
| Cholangitis    | Confirm adequate biliary drainage; use selective antibiotics when drainage is incomplete, active cholangitis is present, the patient is immunocompromised, or biliary stents remain in place; maintain sterile technique.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                        | Broad-spectrum antibiotics and restoration of biliary drainage by ERCP, percutaneous intervention, or surgery when needed.                                                                                                                                    |
